name: AlignOrientation
simple: AlignOrientation turns a part to face a goal direction and keeps it facing that way. The goal can be another attachment's direction or a rotation you type in. It only turns the part; it does not move it. For moving, use AlignPosition.
analogy: AlignOrientation is like a compass needle or a sunflower: wherever it is, it keeps turning to point the right way.
whenToUse: Keep a vehicle or hoverboard upright
Make a turret or pet face a target
Rotate a floating platform smoothly to a new angle
Pair with AlignPosition for full physics-based control
where: Create with Instance.new("AlignOrientation"), set Attachment0 to an attachment in the part to turn, then set Attachment1 (copy that attachment's direction) or Mode = OneAttachment and use CFrame. Usually from a Script on the server.

terms.torque: A twisting push that makes things spin, like turning a doorknob or a steering wheel. Torque = force x distance from the spinning point, so pushing farther from the center twists harder.
terms.angular velocity: How fast something spins, and around which axis, measured in radians per second. 2 x pi (about 6.28) radians per second is one full turn every second.
terms.radians: Another way to measure angles. A full circle is 2 x pi (about 6.28) radians, which is 360 degrees. `math.rad(90)` turns 90 degrees into radians.
terms.CFrame: A position plus a rotation in one value. It says where something is and which way it faces.
terms.Vector3: Three numbers (X, Y, Z) bundled together. Used for positions, directions, forces and speeds. Y is up.
terms.attachment: A tiny invisible point you put inside a part. It has a position AND a direction (its own X, Y and Z arrows). Constraints grab parts by their attachments.
terms.Attachment0 / Attachment1: The two attachments a constraint connects. Attachment0 is usually the one that gets pushed or moved; Attachment1 is the other end or the goal.
terms.unanchored: A part that physics is allowed to move. Constraints that push or pull only work on unanchored parts.
terms.center of mass: The balance point of an object. Pushing exactly through it moves the object without spinning it; pushing off to the side also makes it spin.
terms.world space: Directions measured using the whole game world's fixed arrows: Y is always straight up toward the sky, no matter how a part is turned.
terms.Responsiveness: How quickly an Align constraint tries to reach its goal, from 5 (slow and gentle) to 200 (fast and snappy).
terms.axis: An imaginary line something turns around or slides along. An attachment's X axis is its main arrow.
terms.deprecated: Old and replaced by something better. It may still work, but you should not use it in new games.
terms.replicate: Copy from the server to every player's computer automatically. A property marked 'not replicated' is not copied.
terms.orientation: Which way something is turned or facing.
terms.primary axis: An attachment's main arrow (its X direction). The secondary axis is its Y direction.
terms.AlignType: Picks how strict the turning is: AllAxes (match the full rotation), PrimaryAxisParallel (only make the main arrows point the same way), PrimaryAxisPerpendicular (make them point at right angles), PrimaryAxisLookAt (point the main arrow at a spot).
terms.MaxTorque: The most twisting strength it may use to turn the part.
terms.MaxAngularVelocity: The fastest it may spin (radians per second) while turning toward the goal.

examples.title: Turn a floating part to face a new direction
examples.code:
local part = Instance.new("Part")
part.Size = Vector3.new(4, 1, 2)
part.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
part.Anchored = false
part.Parent = workspace

local attachment = Instance.new("Attachment")
attachment.Parent = part

-- Keep it floating in place
local hold = Instance.new("AlignPosition")
hold.Attachment0 = attachment
hold.Mode = Enum.PositionAlignmentMode.OneAttachment
hold.Position = part.Position
hold.MaxForce = 100000
hold.Parent = part

local turn = Instance.new("AlignOrientation")
turn.Attachment0 = attachment
turn.Mode = Enum.OrientationAlignmentMode.OneAttachment
turn.Responsiveness = 15
turn.MaxTorque = 100000
turn.Parent = part

-- Every 2 seconds, turn another 90 degrees around the up axis
local angle = 0
while true do
	angle += 90
	turn.CFrame = CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(angle), 0)
	task.wait(2)
end
explain: AlignPosition holds the part in the air; AlignOrientation only handles the turning.
In OneAttachment mode, the goal rotation comes from the CFrame property. Only its rotation is used; its position is ignored.
CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(90), 0) means 'turned 90 degrees around Y'. math.rad converts degrees to radians.
Each loop adds 90 degrees, so the part smoothly turns a quarter turn every 2 seconds.

gotchas: CFrame, PrimaryAxis, SecondaryAxis and LookAtPosition only matter when Mode is OneAttachment.
If the part turns too slowly or not at all, raise MaxTorque (or Responsiveness).
AlignOrientation does not hold a part up. A loose part will still fall unless something else holds it.
Angles in CFrame.Angles are radians. Use math.rad(degrees).

AlignOrientation.AlignType.simple: How the part should line up with the goal: AllAxes (match the full rotation exactly), PrimaryAxisParallel (main arrows point the same way, free to roll around it), PrimaryAxisPerpendicular (main arrows at a right angle), or PrimaryAxisLookAt (point the main arrow at LookAtPosition).

AlignOrientation.CFrame.simple: The goal rotation, when Mode is OneAttachment. Only the rotation part is used; the position inside the CFrame is ignored.

AlignOrientation.LookAtPosition.simple: A spot in the world for the main arrow to point at. Only used when AlignType is PrimaryAxisLookAt and Mode is OneAttachment. Not copied to players' devices automatically (not replicated).
AlignOrientation.LookAtPosition.example:
local turn = workspace.Turret.AlignOrientation
turn.Mode = Enum.OrientationAlignmentMode.OneAttachment
turn.AlignType = Enum.AlignType.PrimaryAxisLookAt
turn.LookAtPosition = Vector3.new(0, 5, 50) -- aim at this spot

AlignOrientation.MaxAngularVelocity.simple: The fastest it may spin (radians per second) while turning to the goal, when RigidityEnabled is false. A cap, not the exact speed.
AlignOrientation.MaxAngularVelocity.example: workspace.Turret.AlignOrientation.MaxAngularVelocity = math.pi -- at most half a turn per second

AlignOrientation.MaxTorque.simple: The most twisting strength it may use, when RigidityEnabled is false. A cap; Responsiveness decides how much is really used.

AlignOrientation.Mode.simple: TwoAttachment (default): turn Attachment0 to match Attachment1's direction. OneAttachment: ignore Attachment1 and match the CFrame (or PrimaryAxis/SecondaryAxis) property instead.

AlignOrientation.PrimaryAxis.simple: In OneAttachment mode, the direction the goal's main (X) arrow should point, as a length-1 Vector3. Not replicated.

AlignOrientation.PrimaryAxisOnly.simple: Old — use AlignType (PrimaryAxisParallel, PrimaryAxisPerpendicular or PrimaryAxisLookAt) instead.

AlignOrientation.ReactionTorqueEnabled.simple: If false (default), only Attachment0's part is turned. If true, Attachment1's part is twisted the opposite way too.

AlignOrientation.Responsiveness.simple: How quickly it turns to the goal, from 5 (slow and smooth) to 200 (fast and snappy).

AlignOrientation.RigidityEnabled.simple: If true, the physics engine turns the part to the goal as fast and hard as it can, ignoring MaxTorque, MaxAngularVelocity and Responsiveness. If false (default), those settings control it.

AlignOrientation.SecondaryAxis.simple: In OneAttachment mode, the direction the goal's secondary (Y) arrow should point, as a length-1 Vector3. Not replicated.
